The graph above shows $y={f}^{″}(x).$ Find the intervals on which the function $f(x)$ is concave up.
feedback.worked_solution:
A function $f(x)$ is concave up over an interval $(a,b)$ if ${f}^{″}(x)>0$ for all $x\in (a,b).$

On the given graph of $y={f}^{″}(x),$ we can see that ${f}^{″}(x)>0$ on the intervals  $(-1,0)$ and  $(0,1).$  Therefore, the function $f(x)$ is concave up on the intervals  $(-1,0)$ and  $(0,1).$
